lead: An example is run as `nvs run <file>` with no words after it and no terminal, so a feature whose subject is input has to print something when it is given none.
body: `bun nv proofs --run` and `--bless` run an example with a bare argument vector and captured streams (`tools/nv/proofs/run.ts`), and there is no `--ARGS--` section like the one a `.nvst` case has. Write the program the way a real tool behaves with nothing given: an empty list from `Core\Cli::arguments`, a prompt taking its `{default: …}`, a `colorDepth()` of `None`.
